Company: Lumina Dynamics
Sector: Retail & Wholesale Trade
Size: Micro

Company Description: Lumina Dynamics is a specialty coffee and gourmet food retailer operating six physical locations, underpinned by an e-commerce channel. The company focuses on high-margin, artisanal products, maintaining in-house roasting capabilities and curating over 200 unique items to serve discerning urban customers. Currently, the core challenge lies in scaling operational efficiency and building a robust subscription loyalty framework.

Innovation Process: formal
Digital Maturity: 3/4
Customer Feedback: dedicated_research

Strategic Goals: We are heavily dependent on our top three product categories and concentrated customer base, creating significant revenue vulnerability. Our primary goal is aggressive diversification by identifying adjacent market segments—including new wholesale partners or entirely new private-label food lines—to reduce single-source risk.
Strategic Priority: diversification
Time Horizon: medium
Risk Appetite: conservative

Team Size: We have 2 generalist developers who split their time between maintaining our existing systems, handling customer support escalations, and occasionally prototyping new features. There is no dedicated innovation or R&D role — innovation happens when these developers have spare cycles between urgent operational tasks, which is rare.
Revenue Range: 1m_to_10m
Estimated Innovation Budget: ~EUR165,000/year (3% of revenue)
Decision Making: small_leadership_team

Main Barriers: budget, talent, time
Competitive Pressure: high
Regulatory Environment: low

Past Initiatives: Innovation is embedded in our operating rhythm through structured quarterly hackathons and a formal patent portfolio management system. We also utilize a rotating 'innovation fellow' program to dedicate high-potential employees to exploratory projects, demonstrating a commitment to continuous learning and process improvement.
Additional Context: Operating in a high-pressure specialty food market requires constant adaptation to evolving sourcing costs and consumer trends. The current lean structure means innovation relies heavily on maximizing the output of existing operational staff.
